gap: Headings don't hang their markers: A's `##` sits at x=694, flush with the body's left edge (694–697), so the heading's actual words start at x=775 — 81px (≈40 CSS px, 3.3 characters) inside the column. B outdents `##` to x=619 so "1. Down the Rabbit Hole" lands on the same 691px edge as the prose. Every heading in A therefore puts a visible step in the left edge; the one line on the page that should anchor the column is the one line that doesn't.
gapTheirs: The focus zone is coloured confetti: 25.0% of the ink pixels in B's active band are chromatic (ochre ~#a0681c on "small"/"small"/"attractive", blue ~#3060a8 on "finds"/"fit"/"sees", green on "but"), against 0.0% in A — A's focused sentence is one flat neutral #1c1c1c. Six words of a single sentence are broken into three hues at exactly the point of maximum attention.
verdict: A is the page you can actually write on: neutral #f9f9f9 paper, a dead-straight body edge at 694px, and a three-step focus ramp (#cccccc far context → #b2b2b2 approaching the caret → #1c1c1c live sentence) that tells you where you are without shouting. B throws that away for a rainbow — a quarter of the ink you're currently typing rendered in ochre, blue and green, plus a struck-through word — which is a syntax highlighter's idea of calm, not a writer's. B also can't hold its measure: its italic isn't metric-compatible with its roman, so the wrap boundary jumps from x≈2176 in the emphasised block to x≈2225 in the plain one, a 49px (≈2 character) swing down the page, where A's two blocks agree to 1px (2213 vs 2212). B wins the hanging `##` and gives marginally more air (line pitch 73.3 vs 72, ≈1.81 vs 1.74 line-height), and neither app dims its markdown markers at all — but a 40px heading step is a flaw you stop seeing by page three, and coloured words under the caret is one you never stop seeing.

builderNote: Rebuilt app/css/page.css around measurements of the iA window (column 768 logical px = 64 chars, margins 347 each side, first ink 85px below the editor top, blank line = exactly one pitch): the page now centres type.css's 64ch measure and opens the document two line-pitches from the top instead of the old 40vh slab, so the first sentence lands under your eyes; typewriter mode swaps to 52vh/62vh padding so any line can still reach the middle. Added scroll-padding (10vh/28vh) — verified Chromium honours it for textarea caret scrolling, so typing at the end of a document rests at ~69% of the window instead of the bottom edge — plus scrollbar-gutter: stable both-edges so the column never shifts sideways when a doc grows past one screen (measured left 336.0 / right 336.0 both ways), and a faint ":has()"-driven "Start writing…" on the empty page, sitting exactly where the first glyph will land (A/B'd: no typing-latency cost). Ours now matches the reference to within 2 logical px on first-ink height and 1px on column edges; remaining differences in the pair are other pieces' (syntax colours, hanging ## which this architecture cannot do).
secondary: Unstable measure in B: italic block wraps at x≈2176, roman block at x≈2225 — a 49px (~2ch) shift in the right rag between paragraphs; A holds 2213/2212 (1px).

Both dim context to near-illegibility: A's far tier #cccccc on #f9f9f9 is ~1.50:1 contrast, B's flat #c4c5c5 on #f6f7f7 ~1.59:1. A's middle tier (#b2b2b2, ~2.00:1) at least makes the preceding sentence readable; B has no middle tier.
Neither dims the `##`: A's marker and heading words are both exactly #cccccc, B's both #c4c5c5 — the syntax weighs the same as the prose in both.
Carets are a wash: 6px wide (3 CSS px) in both, 72px vs 70px tall, #00b5ff vs #00bfff.
Measure is comfortable in both — ~62ch (A) vs ~64ch (B) at a mono advance of ~24.8 vs ~24.3px; not a differentiator.
Top of text sits at y=166 (A) / y=170 (B) — ~84 CSS px. Both are tight above the first heading; neither frames the opening line with any real air.
Paragraph separation: A adds ~39px over its 72px line pitch, B ~49px over 73px. B's block rhythm is slightly clearer, A's slightly cramped.
